newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka forces close in on Tamil rebel base.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka forces close in on Tamil rebel base.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops advanced slowly towards a key northern town on Thursday under a shower of rocket-propelled grenades and mortar rounds launched by the Tamil Tiger defenders, the Defence Ministry said.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam, fighting a 13-year war for a homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east, said in their daily radio broadcast that they were engaging the troops with "increased fierceness."
A military spokesman said the rebels were putting up stiff resistance with heavy rocket-propelled grenade and mortar fire.

More than 30 LTTE rebels were killed and 50 wounded in fierce fighting on Wednesday, the fourth day of the army's pincer offensive on Kilinochchi, 285 km (180 miles) north of Colombo, a ministry statement said.

The Defence Ministry said 13 soldiers also were killed and 30 wounded, raising the army's the death toll to 71 and the number of wounded to 145 since the offensive was launched on Sunday after more than a month-long lull.
Government statistics put the Tigers' casualties at around 530 dead or wounded.
But army sources said radio communications by the LTTE monitored by the military said only 61 guerrillas, including 23 officers, had been killed.

A military spokesman said two columns of troops made progress in their advance from the road junction town of Paranthan, six km (four miles) north of Kilinochchi, approaching the rebel base from different directions.
He said the troops were dominating the newly captured area on its eastern flank, but rebel resistance had limited army progress to one km (half a mile) overnight.
"Latest reports indicate that terrorists launched a massive counter-attack during the very early hours of (Thursday)," the ministry statement said of the fighting on the western flank.
"The counter-attack has been repulsed effectively causing very heavy casualties among the terrorists," it said.
It did not say how many rebels were killed on Thursday.
Relief workers in the northern frontline town of Vavuniya told Reuters that tens of thousands of civilians displaced by the current wave of fighting were moving to safer areas south of Kilinochchi.
"People are seen on the roads moving in a hurry, trying to escape shell attacks and air attacks," one relief worker said.
International aid workers said they were unable to verify the number of displaced people.
"We hear there are movements, but at this stage we are not able to assess the magnitude of the movement," an International Committee of the Red Cross official said.

The LTTE, in a statement issued to international news agencies from their London office, said five civilians on the road were killed and 15 wounded when air force bombers attacked a crowd of fleeing refugees at Puthumurippu, near Kilinochchi.
"The bodies of the five people were blown into pieces beyond recognition," the statement said.
A military spokesman in Colombo said he was unaware of the incident.
It was not possible to verify the claim as the government has banned journalists from visiting the war zone.
The armed forces have targeted Kilinochchi since the Tigers overran the military's northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing almost its entire garrison of more than 1,000 men.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the conflict since it began in 1983.
